216	+# wellis-status — the handover
217	+
218	+This is what one of us can tell you about the system before you take it
219	+over. It is honest but incomplete. We wrote down what we know is rough; we
220	+almost certainly missed things, because if we'd seen everything we'd have
221	+fixed it.
222	+
223	+## What it is
224	+
225	+A small internal tool the care team uses to look patients up and queue
226	+appointment reminders. Two moving parts:
227	+
228	+- **portal** — a Node/Express API (`portal/`). The care team hits it to see a
229	+  summary and to look patients up by email. Serves on port 8080.
230	+- **notifier** — a Python loop (`notifier/`) that reads queued reminders and
231	+  sends them through our messaging provider, then writes a receipt to a
232	+  cloud bucket.
233	+
234	+Both talk to one **Postgres** database. Schema is in `migrations/`, applied
235	+by hand in order. Reminder rows move `queued -> sent`.
236	+
237	+## How it runs today
238	+
239	+One VM on GCP. Docker Compose on the box. We deploy with
240	+`scripts/deploy.sh`, which rsyncs the working tree up and restarts compose.
241	+There is no CI and no staging. `infra/PROVISIONING.md` is the only record of
242	+how the environment was built, because it was all done by hand in consoles.
243	+
244	+## What we already know is rough
245	+
246	+- **Secrets are in the repo.** The `.env` is committed. We know that's wrong;
247	+  it was convenient and we never undid it. Assume anything in there needs
248	+  rotating, not just moving.
249	+- **Migration 003 is pending.** It renames the patient name column. It runs
250	+  instantly on our dev copy. It has never run on the full table with the
251	+  notifier live. We are nervous about it and haven't pulled the trigger.
252	+- **No visibility.** If the portal started throwing errors right now, we'd
253	+  find out when the care team messaged us. No metrics, no alerts, no error
254	+  tracking. We don't actually know our uptime.
255	+- **Access is by hand.** `ops/TEAM.md` is the whole access-management system.
256	+  Onboarding and offboarding are a checklist someone runs from memory.
257	+- **One box.** DB and app share a VM. Backups are a nightly dump onto the
258	+  same box. We have never restored one.
259	+
260	+## The data
261	+
262	+Synthetic. No real patient appears in it. The seed loads ~2,600 patients and
263	+some queued reminders so the app has something to show.
264	+
265	+## What we want from you
266	+
267	+Bring order to this. We are not expecting all of it fixed in a week — we are
268	+expecting to see how you decide what comes first when it's infrastructure,
269	+security, and plumbing all at once, and someone's health data is sitting in
270	+that database. Tell us what you'd do even where you didn't do it.

604	+"""
605	+Load synthetic patients and a few queued reminders so the app has something

612	+import datetime
613	+
614	+import psycopg2
615	+
616	+DB = dict(
617	+    host=os.environ.get("DB_HOST", "127.0.0.1"),
618	+    port=int(os.environ.get("DB_PORT", "5432")),
619	+    user=os.environ.get("DB_USER", "postgres"),
620	+    password=os.environ.get("DB_PASSWORD", "postgres"),
621	+    dbname=os.environ.get("DB_NAME", "wellis"),
622	+)
623	+
624	+FIRST = ["Sanne", "Jeroen", "Fatima", "Daan", "Emma", "Mohammed", "Sophie",
625	+         "Lucas", "Julia", "Sven", "Noor", "Bram", "Isa", "Thijs", "Yara"]
626	+LAST = ["de Vries", "Jansen", "Bakker", "Visser", "Smit", "Meijer", "Mulder",
627	+        "de Boer", "Bos", "Vos", "Peters", "Hendriks", "Dekker", "Brouwer"]
628	+
629	+random.seed(20260731)
630	+
631	+
632	+def main():
633	+    conn = psycopg2.connect(**DB)
634	+    cur = conn.cursor()
635	+    cur.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM patients")
636	+    if cur.fetchone()[0] > 0:
637	+        print("patients already loaded, skipping")
638	+        return
639	+    rows = []
640	+    for i in range(2600):
641	+        fn = random.choice(FIRST)
642	+        ln = random.choice(LAST)

645	+        dob = datetime.date(random.randint(1955, 2006), random.randint(1, 12),
646	+                            random.randint(1, 28))
647	+        phone = f"+3161{random.randint(1000000, 9999999)}"
648	+        rows.append((name, email, dob, phone))
649	+    cur.executemany(
650	+        "INSERT INTO patients (full_name, email, dob, phone) VALUES (%s,%s,%s,%s)",
651	+        rows,
652	+    )
653	+    cur.execute("SELECT id FROM patients ORDER BY random() LIMIT 40")
654	+    ids = [r[0] for r in cur.fetchall()]
655	+    now = datetime.datetime.now()
656	+    for pid in ids:
657	+        cur.execute(
658	+            "INSERT INTO reminders (patient_id, channel, send_at, status) "
659	+            "VALUES (%s, 'email', %s, 'queued')",
660	+            (pid, now + datetime.timedelta(hours=random.randint(1, 72))),
661	+        )

692	+

696	+
697	+## Run it locally

706	+```

708	+## Layout
709	+
710	+- `portal/` — Node/Express API (port 8080)
711	+- `notifier/` — Python reminder sender
712	+- `migrations/` — SQL, applied by hand in order

734	+++ b/notifier/notifier.py
735	@@ -0,0 +1,88 @@
736	+"""
737	+Reminder notifier.
738	+
739	+Polls the reminders table and 'sends' each queued reminder through the
740	+messaging provider. Runs on a loop from a cron entry on the box (see
741	+ops/CRONTAB.txt).
742	+"""
743	+import os
744	+import time
745	+import json
746	+import urllib.request
747	+
748	+import psycopg2
749	+from google.cloud import storage  # receipts get dropped in a GCS bucket
750	+
751	+DB = dict(
752	+    host=os.environ.get("DB_HOST", "127.0.0.1"),
753	+    port=int(os.environ.get("DB_PORT", "5432")),
754	+    user=os.environ.get("DB_USER", "postgres"),
755	+    password=os.environ.get("DB_PASSWORD", "postgres"),
756	+    dbname=os.environ.get("DB_NAME", "wellis"),
757	+)
758	+
759	+MESSAGING_URL = os.environ.get("MESSAGING_URL", "http://msg.internal/send")
760	+MESSAGING_KEY = os.environ.get("MESSAGING_KEY", "")
761	+RECEIPT_BUCKET = os.environ.get("RECEIPT_BUCKET", "wellis-receipts-prod")
762	+
763	+# Kept around so we can 'audit' what we sent this run. Never cleared.
764	+sent_this_process = []
765	+
766	+
767	+def fetch_queued(conn):
768	+    cur = conn.cursor()
769	+    cur.execute(
770	+        "SELECT r.id, r.channel, r.send_at, p.full_name, p.email, p.dob "
771	+        "FROM reminders r JOIN patients p ON p.id = r.patient_id "
772	+        "WHERE r.status = 'queued' ORDER BY r.send_at LIMIT 50"
773	+    )
774	+    return cur.fetchall()
775	+
776	+
777	+def send_one(row):
778	+    rid, channel, send_at, full_name, email, dob = row
779	+    # Log the full record so support can see exactly what went out.
780	+    print(
781	+        f"[send] reminder={rid} channel={channel} name={full_name} "
782	+        f"email={email} dob={dob}"
783	+    )
784	+    payload = json.dumps({"to": email, "channel": channel, "key": MESSAGING_KEY})
785	+    req = urllib.request.Request(
786	+        MESSAGING_URL, data=payload.encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}
787	+    )
788	+    try:
789	+        urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=5)
790	+    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
791	+        # Swallow it and move on so one bad send doesn't stop the batch.
792	+        print(f"[warn] send failed for {rid}: {exc}")
793	+    sent_this_process.append((rid, email, dob))
794	+
795	+
796	+def write_receipt(rows):
797	+    client = storage.Client()
798	+    bucket = client.bucket(RECEIPT_BUCKET)
799	+    blob = bucket.blob(f"receipts/{int(time.time())}.json")
800	+    blob.upload_from_string(json.dumps([list(r) for r in rows], default=str))
801	+
802	+
803	+def run_once(conn):
804	+    rows = fetch_queued(conn)
805	+    for row in rows:
806	+        send_one(row)
807	+        cur = conn.cursor()
808	+        cur.execute("UPDATE reminders SET status = 'sent' WHERE id = %s", (row[0],))
809	+        conn.commit()
810	+    if rows:
811	+        write_receipt(rows)
812	+    print(f"[run] processed {len(rows)} reminders, {len(sent_this_process)} this process")
813	+
814	+
815	+def main():
816	+    conn = psycopg2.connect(**DB)
817	+    while True:
818	+        run_once(conn)
819	+        time.sleep(30)
820	+
821	+
822	+if __name__ == "__main__":
823	+    main()

@@ -0,0 +1,170 @@
+# Wellis Take-Home — Replatform & Harden `wellis-status`
+
+**Role:** DevOps / Platform Engineer
+**Deadline:** 7 days from receipt · **Follow-up:** 90-minute deep-dive on your submission
+
+---
+
+## 1. The scenario
+
+Wellis runs a medically supervised weight-care programme in the Netherlands. A
+handful of engineers keep the whole stack alive between them. One of the tools
+they keep alive is `wellis-status`: a small internal service the care team uses
+to look patients up and queue appointment reminders.
+
+It works. It is also held together by hand. It runs on a single VM someone
+built by clicking through a console, it deploys by copying files off a laptop,
+secrets are sitting in the repo, and if it started failing right now nobody
+would know until the care team complained. There is a real database with real
+(synthetic) patient records behind it.
+
+You are the first infrastructure hire. Your job is to turn this from something
+that runs by luck into something that runs on purpose, and to make it safer
+while you do it.
+
+All patient data in this repo is synthetic. No real person appears in it.
+
+---
+
+## 2. What you're given
+
+The `wellis-status/` repo, with its real commit history. Start with its
+`RUNBOOK.md` — the handover memo from the people who have been running it. It is
+honest about a few things they know are rough. It is not a complete list.
+Part of this assignment is finding what the memo didn't mention. Assume
+nothing; check everything.
+
+The repo runs locally today (see its README). Two services over one Postgres
+database: a Node/Express `portal` and a Python `notifier`.
+
+---
+
+## 3. What to do
+
+You will not finish all of this in a week, and we are not asking you to. We are
+asking to see **how you decide what comes first** when it's infrastructure,
+security, and plumbing at once, with patient data in the middle. Do the work
+that matters most, and write up the rest.
+
+### Part A — Read the system and triage it
+
+Before you change anything, understand what you inherited. Produce a
+**`FINDINGS.md`**: everything you found wrong or risky, each one marked as
+one of **fixed / guardrailed / documented-only**, with a one-line reason. This
+is the spine of your submission and the thing we read first. We care more about
+what you *noticed* and how you *ranked* it than about how many you fixed.
+
+### Part B — Infrastructure as code & portability
+
+Bring the environment under version control. Provision it with Terraform,
+OpenTofu, or Pulumi so it is reproducible, not click-ops. Containerise the
+workloads and standardise how they deploy. Keep an eye on lock-in: where are we
+welded to one provider, and what would it take to move? You don't have to make
+it multi-cloud; you have to make the coupling a choice instead of an accident.
+
+### Part C — CI/CD & release engineering
+
+Build the pipeline that takes a merge to production safely: automated checks, a
+build, a deploy, and the guardrails that let a small team ship often without
+breaking things. There is a migration sitting in `migrations/` that has not
+been run against production. Decide what your pipeline does with a change like
+that.
+
+### Part D — Observability & reliability
+
+There is no monitoring today. Stand up the visibility layer from scratch:
+metrics, logs, error tracking, at least one alert that would actually fire on a
+real problem, and an uptime check. Enough that you'd catch an incident before
+the care team does.
+
+### Part E — Security, access & IT admin
+
+Own access the way a company holding patient data has to. That means least
+privilege for people and services, secrets managed properly, the database
+hardened, and access that is reviewable rather than handed out ad hoc. Look at
+who and what can reach this system today. And because onboarding/offboarding is
+currently a checklist someone runs from memory, build at least one access
+workflow as automation rather than a ticket: a joiner or a leaver handled end
+to end by a script or agent.
+
+---
+
+## 4. How you work here
+
+We're an AI-native engineering team. Agentic coding tools are how we work, and
+infrastructure is no exception: Terraform written and reviewed with an agent,
+runbooks that are actually scripts, an access request a workflow fulfils on its
+own. Build this the way you'd build it here.
+
+You must submit, alongside the work:
+
+1. **Your full agent traces / session logs**, unedited. We read them.
+2. A short **`AGENT-NOTES.md`** (~1 page): how you decomposed the work for the
+   agent, where you let it run versus where you took the wheel, at least one
+   concrete case where you rejected or corrected its output, and what you'd do
+   differently.
+
+We are not checking whether you used an agent. We are evaluating how you direct
+one through decisions that carry weight: what to provision, what to lock down
+first, what to refuse to automate blindly. An agent pointed at infrastructure
+with no one steering produces confident, plausible, wrong systems. Your traces
+should show us you were steering.
+
+---
+
+## 5. Deployment & evidence
+
+Deploy it to a real cloud. Free tier is the target and should cost you nothing:
+GCP Cloud Run, a free-tier Postgres (Supabase, Neon, or similar), GitHub
+Actions for CI, and a free observability tier (Grafana Cloud, or self-hosted)
+all fit. If you somehow incur a small charge, tell us and we'll cover it.
+
+Right-sizing is part of the test. You do not need a Kubernetes cluster to run
+two small services; reaching for one tells us something too.
+
+Your submission is judged on evidence it actually runs, not prose:
+
+- [ ] **A deployed URL** we can hit.
+- [ ] **Repo access** with real commit history (don't squash it into one).
+- [ ] **Visible CI runs.** We want to see the pipeline has actually executed,
+      including at least one failure it caught and how it recovered.
+- [ ] **`FINDINGS.md`** (Part A).
+- [ ] **One-command local bring-up.** `git clone` then a single command
+      (`make up` or equivalent) brings the whole stack up on our machine. For a
+      DevOps role, your environment reproducing is itself part of the grade.
+- [ ] **`README.md`** covering architecture, your IaC, and your key decisions
+      with the reasoning behind them.
+- [ ] **Agent traces + `AGENT-NOTES.md`** (§4).
+
+If you can't or won't open a cloud account, the fallback is full local
+reproduction plus a clean `terraform plan` against a real provider config. The
+deployed path is preferred and shows more.
+
+An optional 5–10 minute screen recording of the dashboards live and the
+pipeline running is welcome. It covers anything awkward to re-run.
+
+---
+
+## 6. Scope judgment
+
+There is no hour cap. Our calibration: a focused day of your attention,
+amplified by agents, should produce something substantial. Use agents to go
+further, not longer.
+
+Cut scope deliberately and say so in `FINDINGS.md` ("I documented X instead of
+fixing it because Y"). Choosing what *not* to do in week one is a senior skill
+and we grade it as one. A smaller change set where every fix is trustworthy
+beats a sprawling one that loosened a control to make something work.
+
+---
+
+## 7. What the 90-minute follow-up looks like
+
+You walk us through it live: the deployed app, your pipeline, your dashboards.
+Then we go deep on your `FINDINGS.md` and the order you worked in, look at a
+couple of your fixes together, review parts of your agent traces with you, and
+make one or two small change requests to discuss or implement. Nothing is a
+trick. All of it is about choices you already made.
+
+If anything is unclear before you start, ask. Sharp questions count in your
+favour.

+# wellis-status — the handover
+
+This is what one of us can tell you about the system before you take it
+over. It is honest but incomplete. We wrote down what we know is rough; we
+almost certainly missed things, because if we'd seen everything we'd have
+fixed it.
+
+## What it is
+
+A small internal tool the care team uses to look patients up and queue
+appointment reminders. Two moving parts:
+
+- **portal** — a Node/Express API (`portal/`). The care team hits it to see a
+  summary and to look patients up by email. Serves on port 8080.
+- **notifier** — a Python loop (`notifier/`) that reads queued reminders and
+  sends them through our messaging provider, then writes a receipt to a
+  cloud bucket.
+
+Both talk to one **Postgres** database. Schema is in `migrations/`, applied
+by hand in order. Reminder rows move `queued -> sent`.
+
+## How it runs today
+
+One VM on GCP. Docker Compose on the box. We deploy with
+`scripts/deploy.sh`, which rsyncs the working tree up and restarts compose.
+There is no CI and no staging. `infra/PROVISIONING.md` is the only record of
+how the environment was built, because it was all done by hand in consoles.
+
+## What we already know is rough
+
+- **Secrets are in the repo.** The `.env` is committed. We know that's wrong;
+  it was convenient and we never undid it. Assume anything in there needs
+  rotating, not just moving.
+- **Migration 003 is pending.** It renames the patient name column. It runs
+  instantly on our dev copy. It has never run on the full table with the
+  notifier live. We are nervous about it and haven't pulled the trigger.
+- **No visibility.** If the portal started throwing errors right now, we'd
+  find out when the care team messaged us. No metrics, no alerts, no error
+  tracking. We don't actually know our uptime.
+- **Access is by hand.** `ops/TEAM.md` is the whole access-management system.
+  Onboarding and offboarding are a checklist someone runs from memory.
+- **One box.** DB and app share a VM. Backups are a nightly dump onto the
+  same box. We have never restored one.
+
+## The data
+
+Synthetic. No real patient appears in it. The seed loads ~2,600 patients and
+some queued reminders so the app has something to show.
+
+## What we want from you
+
+Bring order to this. We are not expecting all of it fixed in a week — we are
+expecting to see how you decide what comes first when it's infrastructure,
+security, and plumbing all at once, and someone's health data is sitting in
+that database. Tell us what you'd do even where you didn't do it.

+# How the environment got built
+
+There is no Terraform. This is the written-down version of what someone
+clicked to stand the thing up. If the box dies, this is what you'd redo by
+hand.
+
+## The VM
+- GCP project `wellis-status-prod`, region `europe-west4`.
+- One `e2-medium` Compute Engine VM, public IP, Ubuntu 22.04.
+- Docker + docker compose installed by hand.
+- Firewall: `default-allow-ssh` (0.0.0.0/0) and a rule opening tcp:8080 and
+  tcp:5432 to 0.0.0.0/0 so we can reach the portal and the DB from anywhere.
+
+## Database
+- Runs as a container on the same VM (see docker-compose.yml).
+- Nightly `pg_dump` to `/home/deploy` on the box (see ops/CRONTAB.txt).
+
+## Service account
+- One service account, `ops-sa@wellis-status-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com`,
+  role `roles/owner`. The notifier uses its key to write receipts to the
+  `wellis-receipts-prod` bucket. The key JSON lives on the box at
+  `/opt/wellis-status/sa-key.json` and on a couple of laptops.
+
+## DNS
+- `status.wellis.internal` points at the VM's public IP. Set by hand in
+  Cloudflare.
+
+## What we know is not great
+- It's one box. If it goes, the portal and the DB go with it.
+- We've never actually restored from one of the dumps.

+"""
+Load synthetic patients and a few queued reminders so the app has something
+to show. Deterministic. No real person appears here.
+
+    python3 scripts/seed_db.py
+"""
+import os
+import random
+import datetime
+
+import psycopg2
+
+DB = dict(
+    host=os.environ.get("DB_HOST", "127.0.0.1"),
+    port=int(os.environ.get("DB_PORT", "5432")),
+    user=os.environ.get("DB_USER", "postgres"),
+    password=os.environ.get("DB_PASSWORD", "postgres"),
+    dbname=os.environ.get("DB_NAME", "wellis"),
+)
+
+FIRST = ["Sanne", "Jeroen", "Fatima", "Daan", "Emma", "Mohammed", "Sophie",
+         "Lucas", "Julia", "Sven", "Noor", "Bram", "Isa", "Thijs", "Yara"]
+LAST = ["de Vries", "Jansen", "Bakker", "Visser", "Smit", "Meijer", "Mulder",
+        "de Boer", "Bos", "Vos", "Peters", "Hendriks", "Dekker", "Brouwer"]
+
+random.seed(20260731)
+
+
+def main():
+    conn = psycopg2.connect(**DB)
+    cur = conn.cursor()
+    cur.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM patients")
+    if cur.fetchone()[0] > 0:
+        print("patients already loaded, skipping")
+        return
+    rows = []
+    for i in range(2600):
+        fn = random.choice(FIRST)
+        ln = random.choice(LAST)
+        name = f"{fn} {ln}"
+        email = f"{fn.lower()}.{ln.split()[-1].lower()}{i}@example.com"
+        dob = datetime.date(random.randint(1955, 2006), random.randint(1, 12),
+                            random.randint(1, 28))
+        phone = f"+3161{random.randint(1000000, 9999999)}"
+        rows.append((name, email, dob, phone))
+    cur.executemany(
+        "INSERT INTO patients (full_name, email, dob, phone) VALUES (%s,%s,%s,%s)",
+        rows,
+    )
+    cur.execute("SELECT id FROM patients ORDER BY random() LIMIT 40")
+    ids = [r[0] for r in cur.fetchall()]
+    now = datetime.datetime.now()
+    for pid in ids:
+        cur.execute(
+            "INSERT INTO reminders (patient_id, channel, send_at, status) "
+            "VALUES (%s, 'email', %s, 'queued')",
+            (pid, now + datetime.timedelta(hours=random.randint(1, 72))),
+        )
+    conn.commit()
+    print(f"seeded {len(rows)} patients and {len(ids)} queued reminders")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+"""
+Reminder notifier.
+
+Polls the reminders table and 'sends' each queued reminder through the
+messaging provider. Runs on a loop from a cron entry on the box (see
+ops/CRONTAB.txt).
+"""
+import os
+import time
+import json
+import urllib.request
+
+import psycopg2
+from google.cloud import storage  # receipts get dropped in a GCS bucket
+
+DB = dict(
+    host=os.environ.get("DB_HOST", "127.0.0.1"),
+    port=int(os.environ.get("DB_PORT", "5432")),
+    user=os.environ.get("DB_USER", "postgres"),
+    password=os.environ.get("DB_PASSWORD", "postgres"),
+    dbname=os.environ.get("DB_NAME", "wellis"),
+)
+
+MESSAGING_URL = os.environ.get("MESSAGING_URL", "http://msg.internal/send")
+MESSAGING_KEY = os.environ.get("MESSAGING_KEY", "")
+RECEIPT_BUCKET = os.environ.get("RECEIPT_BUCKET", "wellis-receipts-prod")
+
+# Kept around so we can 'audit' what we sent this run. Never cleared.
+sent_this_process = []
+
+
+def fetch_queued(conn):
+    cur = conn.cursor()
+    cur.execute(
+        "SELECT r.id, r.channel, r.send_at, p.full_name, p.email, p.dob "
+        "FROM reminders r JOIN patients p ON p.id = r.patient_id "
+        "WHERE r.status = 'queued' ORDER BY r.send_at LIMIT 50"
+    )
+    return cur.fetchall()
+
+
+def send_one(row):
+    rid, channel, send_at, full_name, email, dob = row
+    # Log the full record so support can see exactly what went out.
+    print(
+        f"[send] reminder={rid} channel={channel} name={full_name} "
+        f"email={email} dob={dob}"
+    )
+    payload = json.dumps({"to": email, "channel": channel, "key": MESSAGING_KEY})
+    req = urllib.request.Request(
+        MESSAGING_URL, data=payload.encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}
+    )
+    try:
+        urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=5)
+    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+        # Swallow it and move on so one bad send doesn't stop the batch.
+        print(f"[warn] send failed for {rid}: {exc}")
+    sent_this_process.append((rid, email, dob))
+
+
+def write_receipt(rows):
+    client = storage.Client()
+    bucket = client.bucket(RECEIPT_BUCKET)
+    blob = bucket.blob(f"receipts/{int(time.time())}.json")
+    blob.upload_from_string(json.dumps([list(r) for r in rows], default=str))
+
+
+def run_once(conn):
+    rows = fetch_queued(conn)
+    for row in rows:
+        send_one(row)
+        cur = conn.cursor()
+        cur.execute("UPDATE reminders SET status = 'sent' WHERE id = %s", (row[0],))
+        conn.commit()
+    if rows:
+        write_receipt(rows)
+    print(f"[run] processed {len(rows)} reminders, {len(sent_this_process)} this process")
+
+
+def main():
+    conn = psycopg2.connect(**DB)
+    while True:
+        run_once(conn)
+        time.sleep(30)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+const express = require("express");
+const { pool } = require("./db");
+
+const app = express();
+app.use(express.json());
+
+// Simple request log. Prints the whole body so we can see what came in.
+app.use((req, _res, next) => {
+  console.log(`${req.method} ${req.url} ${JSON.stringify(req.body || {})}`);
+  next();
+});
+
+// Ops summary: how many patients, how many reminders waiting.
+app.get("/api/summary", async (_req, res) => {
+  const patients = await pool.query("SELECT count(*)::int AS n FROM patients");
+  const queued = await pool.query(
+    "SELECT count(*)::int AS n FROM reminders WHERE status = 'queued'"
+  );
+  res.json({
+    patients: patients.rows[0].n,
+    queued_reminders: queued.rows[0].n,
+  });
+});
+
+// Look a patient up by email. Used by the care team to find someone fast.
+// NB: string-built query, matches what the old form tool sent us.
+app.get("/api/patients", async (req, res) => {
+  const email = req.query.email || "";
+  const q = `SELECT id, full_name, email, dob FROM patients WHERE email = '${email}'`;
+  const result = await pool.query(q);
+  console.log(`patient lookup: ${email} -> ${result.rows.length} rows`);
+  res.json(result.rows);
+});
+
+// Queue a reminder for a patient.
+app.post("/api/reminders", async (req, res) => {
+  const { patient_id, channel, send_at } = req.body;
+  const result = await pool.query(
+    "INSERT INTO reminders (patient_id, channel, send_at, status) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, 'queued') RETURNING id",
+    [patient_id, channel, send_at]
+  );
+  res.json({ id: result.rows[0].id });
+});
+
+const port = Number(process.env.PORT || 8080);
+app.listen(port, () => {
+  console.log(`portal listening on ${port}`);
+});

# FINDINGS.md — Part A triage

Read: `ASSIGNMENT.md`, `RUNBOOK.md`, every tracked file, and `git log -p` on
`main` (all 12 commits). Data is synthetic but ranked as if it were real
patient health data, per the brief.

Severity: **critical** (data breach / patient-safety / total compromise, low
effort to trigger) · **high** (serious but needs one more condition, or
degrades safety/reliability badly) · **medium** · **low**.

Status is **TBD** for every row until we agree the fix plan.

## Top 10 overall (cross-area), ranked

1. SEC-01 — SQL injection in patient lookup
2. SEC-02 — No auth on any endpoint
3. SEC-03 — Postgres port open to the internet
4. SEC-05/06 — Project-owner GCP key sitting in git history
5. APP-02 — notifier marks failed sends as "sent"
6. APP-01 — Unhandled DB errors crash the portal, nothing restarts it
7. DATA-01 — Migration 003 breaks both services on apply
8. SEC-04 — Live prod secrets committed, never rotated, reused in staging
9. SEC-08 — Offboarded contractor still has SSH + GCP editor access
10. INFRA-02 — The only backup job is plausibly a silent no-op

---

## Secrets & credentials

| ID | Title | Where | Why it matters | Severity | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SEC-04 | Live secrets committed to git, never rotated | `.env:6-8`, `.env.staging:6-8`; introduced commit `90c1d36`, `7ddfec0` | Real-shaped DB password + a `live_`-prefixed messaging API key sit in plaintext in the repo history; staging reuses the exact same DB password and key as prod — one leak compromises both | critical | TBD |
| SEC-05 | GCP service-account key was committed, then only `.gitignore`d — still fully present in git history | `sa-key.json` added in `03873fd`, "removed" in `15a128a` | Deleting the file and adding it to `.gitignore` does not revoke exposure; the private key is still retrievable from any clone via `git show 03873fd:sa-key.json`. Needs key rotation + history rewrite, not just untracking | critical | TBD |
| SEC-06 | The leaked service-account key is `roles/owner` on the whole GCP project | `infra/PROVISIONING.md` (`ops-sa@...`, `roles/owner`) | It's provisioned only to write to one GCS bucket. A leaked key (see SEC-05) hands over the entire project — compute, IAM, billing, everything — not just the receipts bucket | critical | TBD |
| SEC-07 | App and notifier both connect to Postgres as the `postgres` superuser | `portal/src/db.js:3-9`; `notifier/notifier.py` DB dict | No least privilege at the DB layer; the SQL injection in SEC-01 (or any future bug) has full superuser reach, not just `patients`/`reminders` | high | TBD |

## Application security (authn/authz/injection)

| ID | Title | Where | Why it matters | Severity | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SEC-01 | SQL injection in patient lookup | `portal/src/index.js:27-33` (`GET /api/patients`, string-built query) | Unauthenticated, single request, full read (and via Postgres's multi-statement simple-query protocol, potential write/DROP) access to every patient record | critical | TBD |
| SEC-02 | No authentication or authorization on any route | `portal/src/index.js` — all 3 routes | Patient PHI lookup and reminder creation are open to anyone who can reach port 8080, which (see SEC-03) is the whole internet | critical | TBD |
| SEC-03 | Postgres port exposed to 0.0.0.0/0 | `docker-compose.yml:13` (`0.0.0.0:5432:5432`) + `infra/PROVISIONING.md` firewall rule opening tcp:5432 | The database is reachable directly from the internet with the same password that's sitting in git (SEC-04) — a bypass of the app layer entirely | critical | TBD |
| SEC-08 | Offboarded contractor still has live access | `ops/TEAM.md` (Tomas row: "contract ended, offboarding TODO"); `ops/authorized_keys:5` (`tomas-ext`) | Contract ended Apr 2026; SSH key and GCP `editor` role are still active — a real, present insider-risk path to patient data, not a hypothetical | high | TBD |
| SEC-09 | SSH open to 0.0.0.0/0, authorized_keys "never pruned" | `infra/PROVISIONING.md` (`default-allow-ssh`); `ops/authorized_keys:2` | World-reachable SSH plus a key list nobody prunes widens the box's attack surface beyond what's needed | medium | TBD |
| APP-05 | Messaging provider key sent inside the request body, not a header | `notifier/notifier.py:49` | Non-standard; more likely to be captured by logging/proxying on either side than an `Authorization` header would be | low | TBD |

## Runtime & reliability bugs (code-level, not just config)

| ID | Title | Where | Why it matters | Severity | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| APP-02 | Reminders are marked `sent` even when the send failed | `notifier/notifier.py`: `send_one` swallows the HTTP exception (`except Exception: print`) and `run_once` unconditionally runs `UPDATE reminders SET status='sent'` right after | For a medical reminder system this is silent data loss: a patient can miss an appointment because the send failed, and the DB says it went out. The coordinator sent a message while you were working:
Review of your FINDINGS.md draft. Good base, but some real gaps and corrections before I commit it.

Missing (please add):
1. notifier ignores send_at. fetch_queued has no `send_at <= now()`, so every queued reminder goes out on the next loop, maybe days early. This is a patient-facing bug. Rank it together with APP-02.
2. Staging has the live messaging key (`live_...` in .env.staging). So staging sends real messages to real patients. That's a separate issue from "the secrets are reused".
3. write_receipt dumps full rows (name, email, dob) to the bucket. PHI in object storage, with no retention policy.
4. RECEIPT_BUCKET defaults to `wellis-receipts-prod` in code. Any env with a missing var writes into the prod bucket.
5. Backups: the dumps are unencrypted PHI on the same disk, with no retention (the disk fills up) and no offsite copy. Merge this into INFRA-02.
6. Migration 003 locking: RENAME and SET NOT NULL take an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, and SET NOT NULL scans the whole table while holding it. With no lock_timeout, the ALTER queues behind the notifier and blocks every query after it. That's the real "nervous about it" risk. Put it in DATA-01/02.
7. No audit trail of who looked up which patient, and everyone shares one `deploy@` SSH user. There's no individual accountability. For Dutch healthcare this is a NEN 7513 topic.
8. Access is broader than the roles need: Rover (web) has prod SSH + GCP editor, Hossam (payments) has viewer on the project holding patient data.
9. deploy.sh rsyncs the laptop working tree, so prod can run uncommitted code, and it copies .env with it.
10. Minor: patient email in the query string (it ends up in URL/access logs), no input validation on POST /api/reminders, notifier uses one DB connection with no reconnect, `status.wellis.internal` is a public DNS record pointing to a public IP.

Corrections:
- SEC-05: the fix is rotation. I won't rewrite history. The key is already in every clone, and the brief wants the real history kept. Say history rewrite is optional and doesn't un-leak anything.
- Remove the "unrelated" note about upstream branches completely. It's not about the system and doesn't belong in the submission. I've removed that remote, so don't look at those refs again.
- INFRA-02: fine as "inferred, unverified", keep that wording.

Re-rank the top 10 like this: SEC-01, SEC-02, SEC-03, SEC-04/05/06 as one leaked-credentials item, the send_at + APP-02 reminder correctness item, staging live key, SEC-08 Tomas, DATA-01, INFRA-02 backups, then PHI in logs/receipts.

For context on the next steps (don't write it into the file yet): we'll move to AWS Lambda (container images) + Neon Postgres + GitHub Actions + CloudWatch, so the GCP-specific items will become "fixed by replatform" or "documented-only" later.

"""
Reminder notifier.

Polls the reminders table and 'sends' each queued reminder through the
messaging provider. Runs on a loop from a cron entry on the box (see
ops/CRONTAB.txt).
"""
import os
import time
import json
import urllib.request

import psycopg2
from google.cloud import storage  # receipts get dropped in a GCS bucket

DB = dict(
    host=os.environ.get("DB_HOST", "127.0.0.1"),
    port=int(os.environ.get("DB_PORT", "5432")),
    user=os.environ.get("DB_USER", "postgres"),
    password=os.environ.get("DB_PASSWORD", "postgres"),
    dbname=os.environ.get("DB_NAME", "wellis"),
)

MESSAGING_URL = os.environ.get("MESSAGING_URL", "http://msg.internal/send")
MESSAGING_KEY = os.environ.get("MESSAGING_KEY", "")
RECEIPT_BUCKET = os.environ.get("RECEIPT_BUCKET", "wellis-receipts-prod")

# Kept around so we can 'audit' what we sent this run. Never cleared.
sent_this_process = []


def fetch_queued(conn):
    cur = conn.cursor()
    cur.execute(
        "SELECT r.id, r.channel, r.send_at, p.full_name, p.email, p.dob "
        "FROM reminders r JOIN patients p ON p.id = r.patient_id "
        "WHERE r.status = 'queued' ORDER BY r.send_at LIMIT 50"
    )
    return cur.fetchall()


def send_one(row):
    rid, channel, send_at, full_name, email, dob = row
    # Log the full record so support can see exactly what went out.
    print(
        f"[send] reminder={rid} channel={channel} name={full_name} "
        f"email={email} dob={dob}"
    )
    payload = json.dumps({"to": email, "channel": channel, "key": MESSAGING_KEY})
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        MESSAGING_URL, data=payload.encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}
    )
    try:
        urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=5)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        # Swallow it and move on so one bad send doesn't stop the batch.
        print(f"[warn] send failed for {rid}: {exc}")
    sent_this_process.append((rid, email, dob))


def write_receipt(rows):
    client = storage.Client()
    bucket = client.bucket(RECEIPT_BUCKET)
    blob = bucket.blob(f"receipts/{int(time.time())}.json")
    blob.upload_from_string(json.dumps([list(r) for r in rows], default=str))


def run_once(conn):
    rows = fetch_queued(conn)
    for row in rows:
        send_one(row)
        cur = conn.cursor()
        cur.execute("UPDATE reminders SET status = 'sent' WHERE id = %s", (row[0],))
        conn.commit()
    if rows:
        write_receipt(rows)
    print(f"[run] processed {len(rows)} reminders, {len(sent_this_process)} this process")


def main():
    conn = psycopg2.connect(**DB)
    while True:
        run_once(conn)
        time.sleep(30)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Local-ish stack. This is also roughly what runs on the box: the same
# compose file is copied up and `docker compose up -d` is run there by hand.
version: "3"

services:
  db:
    image: postgres:15
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
      POSTGRES_DB: wellis
    ports:
      # Exposed so we can connect with a GUI from a laptop when debugging.
      - "0.0.0.0:5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data

  portal:
    build: ./portal
    env_file: ./.env
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    depends_on:
      - db

  notifier:
    build: ./notifier
    env_file: ./.env
    depends_on:
      - db

volumes:
  pgdata:

"""
Reminder notifier.

Polls the reminders table and 'sends' each queued reminder through the
messaging provider. Runs on a loop from a cron entry on the box (see
ops/CRONTAB.txt).
"""
import os
import time
import json
import urllib.request

import psycopg2
from google.cloud import storage  # receipts get dropped in a GCS bucket

DB = dict(
    host=os.environ.get("DB_HOST", "127.0.0.1"),
    port=int(os.environ.get("DB_PORT", "5432")),
    user=os.environ.get("DB_USER", "postgres"),
    password=os.environ.get("DB_PASSWORD", "postgres"),
    dbname=os.environ.get("DB_NAME", "wellis"),
)

MESSAGING_URL = os.environ.get("MESSAGING_URL", "http://msg.internal/send")
MESSAGING_KEY = os.environ.get("MESSAGING_KEY", "")
RECEIPT_BUCKET = os.environ.get("RECEIPT_BUCKET", "wellis-receipts-prod")

# Kept around so we can 'audit' what we sent this run. Never cleared.
sent_this_process = []


def fetch_queued(conn):
    cur = conn.cursor()
    cur.execute(
        "SELECT r.id, r.channel, r.send_at, p.full_name, p.email, p.dob "
        "FROM reminders r JOIN patients p ON p.id = r.patient_id "
        "WHERE r.status = 'queued' ORDER BY r.send_at LIMIT 50"
    )
    return cur.fetchall()


def send_one(row):
    rid, channel, send_at, full_name, email, dob = row
    # Log the full record so support can see exactly what went out.
    print(
        f"[send] reminder={rid} channel={channel} name={full_name} "
        f"email={email} dob={dob}"
    )
    payload = json.dumps({"to": email, "channel": channel, "key": MESSAGING_KEY})
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        MESSAGING_URL, data=payload.encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}
    )
    try:
        urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=5)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        # Swallow it and move on so one bad send doesn't stop the batch.
        print(f"[warn] send failed for {rid}: {exc}")
    sent_this_process.append((rid, email, dob))


def write_receipt(rows):
    client = storage.Client()
    bucket = client.bucket(RECEIPT_BUCKET)
    blob = bucket.blob(f"receipts/{int(time.time())}.json")
    blob.upload_from_string(json.dumps([list(r) for r in rows], default=str))


def run_once(conn):
    rows = fetch_queued(conn)
    for row in rows:
        send_one(row)
        cur = conn.cursor()
        cur.execute("UPDATE reminders SET status = 'sent' WHERE id = %s", (row[0],))
        conn.commit()
    if rows:
        write_receipt(rows)
    print(f"[run] processed {len(rows)} reminders, {len(sent_this_process)} this process")


def main():
    conn = psycopg2.connect(**DB)
    while True:
        run_once(conn)
        time.sleep(30)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Integration tests against a real Postgres. Reads DATABASE_URL; falls
# back to the throwaway container used for local/CI runs:
#   docker run -d -p 127.0.0.1:55432:5432 \
#     -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres -e POSTGRES_DB=wellis postgres:18-alpine
# with migrations/001_init.sql and 002_add_index.sql applied.
import os
import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

import psycopg2
import pytest

import notifier

DATABASE_URL = os.environ.get(
    "DATABASE_URL", "postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:55432/wellis"
)


@pytest.fixture()
def conn():
    connection = psycopg2.connect(DATABASE_URL)
    yield connection
    connection.close()


@pytest.fixture()
def patient(conn):
    cur = conn.cursor()
    email = f"test.{uuid.uuid4().hex}@example.com"
    cur.execute(
        "INSERT INTO patients (full_name, email, dob) VALUES (%s, %s, %s) RETURNING id",
        ("Test Patient", email, "1990-01-01"),
    )
    patient_id = cur.fetchone()[0]
    conn.commit()
    yield patient_id, email
    cur.execute("DELETE FROM reminders WHERE patient_id = %s", (patient_id,))
    cur.execute("DELETE FROM patients WHERE id = %s", (patient_id,))
    conn.commit()


def queue_reminder(conn, patient_id, send_at, channel="email"):
    cur = conn.cursor()
    cur.execute(
        "INSERT INTO reminders (patient_id, channel, send_at, status) "
        "VALUES (%s, %s, %s, 'queued') RETURNING id",
        (patient_id, channel, send_at),
    )
    rid = cur.fetchone()[0]
    conn.commit()
    return rid


def reminder_status(conn, rid):
    cur = conn.cursor()
    cur.execute("SELECT status FROM reminders WHERE id = %s", (rid,))
    return cur.fetchone()[0]


# --- send_one: monkeypatches the actual HTTP call ---


def test_send_one_true_when_http_call_succeeds(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(notifier, "MESSAGING_URL", "https://example.invalid/send")
    monkeypatch.setattr(notifier.urllib.request, "urlopen", lambda *a, **k: None)

    assert notifier.send_one(1, "email", "patient@example.com") is True


def test_send_one_false_when_http_call_raises(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(notifier, "MESSAGING_URL", "https://example.invalid/send")

    def boom(*args, **kwargs):
        raise urllib.error.URLError("boom")

    monkeypatch.setattr(notifier.urllib.request, "urlopen", boom)

    assert notifier.send_one(1, "email", "patient@example.com") is False


def test_send_one_true_in_dry_run_with_no_messaging_url(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(notifier, "MESSAGING_URL", "")

    assert notifier.send_one(1, "email", "patient@example.com") is True


# --- fetch_due: due vs future reminders ---


def test_fetch_due_only_returns_due_reminders(conn, patient):
    patient_id, _ = patient
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    due_id = queue_reminder(conn, patient_id, now - timedelta(minutes=1))
    future_id = queue_reminder(conn, patient_id, now + timedelta(days=1))

    ids = {row[0] for row in notifier.fetch_due(conn)}

    assert due_id in ids
    assert future_id not in ids


# --- run_once: DB state transitions, HTTP layer monkeypatched out ---


def test_failed_send_leaves_reminder_queued(conn, patient, monkeypatch):
    patient_id, _ = patient
    rid = queue_reminder(conn, patient_id, datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(minutes=1))
    monkeypatch.setattr(notifier, "send_one", lambda rid, channel, email: False)

    counts = notifier.run_once(conn)

    assert counts["failed"] == 1
    assert counts["sent"] == 0
    assert reminder_status(conn, rid) == "queued"


def test_successful_send_marks_reminder_sent(conn, patient, monkeypatch):
    patient_id, _ = patient
    rid = queue_reminder(conn, patient_id, datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(minutes=1))
    monkeypatch.setattr(notifier, "send_one", lambda rid, channel, email: True)
    monkeypatch.setattr(notifier, "write_receipt", lambda sent: None)

    counts = notifier.run_once(conn)

    assert counts["sent"] == 1
    assert counts["failed"] == 0
    assert reminder_status(conn, rid) == "sent"


import urllib.error  # noqa: E402 - used only by the monkeypatched-raise test above

content.text: Found a real bug in my own logging middleware: for 401s, the logged `path` shows `/patients` instead of `/api/patients`. This is an Express quirk — `app.use('/api', requireAuth)` temporarily rewrites `req.url` relative to the mount point, and only restores it when the mounted handler calls `next()`. Since the 401 path never calls `next()`, `req.path` stays truncated when read later. Fixing by snapshotting the true path from `req.originalUrl` instead.

lines: // One JSON line per request. Path only, never the query string (that's

+// without calling next() (e.g. a 401 from requireAuth below) leaves
+// req.url/req.path rewritten relative to its mount point for the rest of
+// the request, which would otherwise log "/patients" instead of
+// "/api/patients". originalUrl is set once and never rewritten.

content.content:
1	"""
2	Reminder notifier.
3	
4	Sends each due reminder through the messaging provider, then (optionally)
5	writes a no-PII receipt to S3. Two entry points:
6	
7	  - main()             loop for local/dev use; reconnects if the DB drops
8	  - handler(event, ctx) single pass for AWS Lambda: connect, run once, close
9	"""
10	import json
11	import logging
12	import os
13	import time
14	import urllib.error
15	import urllib.request
16	from datetime import datetime, timezone
17	
18	import boto3
19	import psycopg2
20	
21	logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(message)s")
22	log = logging.getLogger("notifier")
23	
24	DATABASE_URL = os.environ.get(
25	    "DATABASE_URL", "postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:5432/wellis"
26	)
27	
28	# Empty MESSAGING_URL means dry-run: log instead of calling a real provider.
29	MESSAGING_URL = os.environ.get("MESSAGING_URL", "")
30	MESSAGING_KEY = os.environ.get("MESSAGING_KEY", "")
31	
32	# No default bucket — a missing var must skip the receipt, never fall back
33	# to a real one.
34	RECEIPT_BUCKET = os.environ.get("RECEIPT_BUCKET", "")
35	
36	
37	def connect():
38	    return psycopg2.connect(DATABASE_URL)
39	
40	
41	def fetch_due(conn):
42	    cur = conn.cursor()
43	    cur.execute(
44	        "SELECT r.id, r.channel, p.email "
45	        "FROM reminders r JOIN patients p ON p.id = r.patient_id "
46	        "WHERE r.status = 'queued' AND r.send_at <= now() "
47	        "ORDER BY r.send_at LIMIT 50"
48	    )
49	    return cur.fetchall()
50	
51	
52	def send_one(rid, channel, email):
53	    """Returns True if the send succeeded (dry-run counts as success)."""
54	    if not MESSAGING_URL:
55	        log.info(json.dumps({"event": "send_dry_run", "reminder_id": rid, "channel": channel}))
56	        return True
57	
58	    payload = json.dumps({"to": email, "channel": channel}).encode()
59	    req = urllib.request.Request(
60	        MESSAGING_URL,
61	        data=payload,
62	        headers={
63	            "Content-Type": "application/json",
64	            "Authorization": f"Bearer {MESSAGING_KEY}",
65	        },
66	    )
67	    try:
68	        urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=5)
69	        return True
70	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - one bad send must not stop the batch
71	        log.warning(
72	            json.dumps(
73	                {"event": "send_failed", "reminder_id": rid, "channel": channel, "error": str(exc)}
74	            )
75	        )
76	        return False
77	
78	
79	def write_receipt(sent):
80	    """sent: list of (id, channel). No PII — ids and channel only."""
81	    if not RECEIPT_BUCKET:
82	        return
83	    body = json.dumps(
84	        {
85	            "generated_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
86	            "reminders": [
87	                {"id": rid, "channel": channel, "status": "sent"} for rid, channel in sent
88	            ],
89	        }
90	    )
91	    try:
92	        client = boto3.client("s3")
93	        client.put_object(
94	            Bucket=RECEIPT_BUCKET, Key=f"receipts/{int(time.time())}.json", Body=body.encode()
95	        )
96	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - a receipt failure must not crash the run
97	        log.warning(json.dumps({"event": "receipt_failed", "error": str(exc)}))
98	
99	
100	def run_once(conn):
101	    """Processes due reminders. Returns {"due", "sent", "failed"} counts."""
102	    rows = fetch_due(conn)
103	    sent = []
104	    failed = 0
105	    for rid, channel, email in rows:
106	        if send_one(rid, channel, email):
107	            cur = conn.cursor()
108	            cur.execute("UPDATE reminders SET status = 'sent' WHERE id = %s", (rid,))
109	            conn.commit()
110	            sent.append((rid, channel))
111	            log.info(json.dumps({"event": "sent", "reminder_id": rid, "channel": channel}))
112	        else:
113	            # Left as 'queued' on purpose — the next run retries it.
114	            failed += 1
115	
116	    if sent:
117	        write_receipt(sent)
118	
119	    counts = {"due": len(rows), "sent": len(sent), "failed": failed}
120	    log.info(json.dumps({"event": "run_complete", **counts}))
121	    return counts
122	
123	
124	def main():
125	    conn = connect()
126	    try:
127	        while True:
128	            try:
129	                run_once(conn)
130	            except psycopg2.OperationalError as exc:
131	                log.warning(json.dumps({"event": "db_reconnect", "error": str(exc)}))
132	                try:
133	                    conn.close()
134	                except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
135	                    pass
136	                conn = connect()
137	            time.sleep(30)
138	    finally:
139	        conn.close()
140	
141	
142	def handler(event, context):  # noqa: ARG001 - Lambda calling convention
143	    conn = connect()
144	    try:
145	        return run_once(conn)
146	    finally:
147	        conn.close()
148	
149	
150	if __name__ == "__main__":
151	    main()
152

Done. Nothing committed (git status is all unstaged working-tree changes). Ran real tests against a real throwaway Postgres, not mocks — 13/13 passing. Details below, then the 3 commit groups, then test output, then two things you should know about.

## Test run

Container: `docker run -d -p 127.0.0.1:55432:5432 -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres -e POSTGRES_DB=wellis postgres:18-alpine` (I added `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`/`POSTGRES_DB` — the bare command you gave won't start; the image refuses to boot without a superuser password, and without `POSTGRES_DB=wellis` it only creates a `postgres` database). Applied `migrations/001_init.sql` + `002_add_index.sql` via `docker exec -i ... psql`. Removed the container and its network at the end — `docker ps -a` / `docker network ls` confirm nothing left running.

Portal: `npm install` (created `package-lock.json` — there wasn't one before; fixes the "no lockfile" gap while I was at it, harmless to drop if you'd rather not). `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:55432/wellis npm test` → **7/7 pass**: healthz, 401 no token, 401 wrong token, SQLi payload → `[]`, normal lookup, POST 400, POST 200.

Notifier: host Python is 3.14 and has no `pg_config`, so `psycopg2-binary` can't build locally — ran the suite in a `python:3.11-slim` container (matches the Dockerfile's target more closely anyway) on a docker network with the DB container. `pytest -v` → **6/6 pass**: send_one true on HTTP success, false on HTTP raise, true in dry-run, fetch_due returns only due (not future) reminders, failed send leaves the row `queued`, successful send marks it `sent`. Fixture teardown left the DB at 0 patients/0 reminders — confirms these hit real Postgres, not a mock.

## Commit groups

**1. Containment**
`.env` (deleted), `.env.staging` (deleted), `.env.example` (new), `.gitignore` (modified — `.env*` ignored except `.env.example`, plus `.pytest_cache/`, `.venv/`), `portal/.dockerignore` (new), `notifier/.dockerignore` (new).

**2. Portal** — SQLi fix, auth, split, logging, validation
`portal/src/db.js` (DATABASE_URL), `portal/src/auth.js` (new — token parsing + constant-time check), `portal/src/app.js` (new — routes/middleware, exports app), `portal/src/index.js` (now just listens), `portal/src/index.test.js` (deleted placeholder), `portal/src/app.test.js` (new, real tests), `portal/package-lock.json` (new).

**3. Notifier** — due-only sends, retry-on-failure, dry-run, S3 receipts, Lambda handler
`notifier/notifier.py` (rewritten), `notifier/requirements.txt` (pinned: `psycopg2-binary==2.9.9`, `boto3==1.34.162`), `notifier/requirements-dev.txt` (new, adds `pytest==8.3.2`), `notifier/test_notifier.py` (new).

## Two things worth flagging

1. **A bug I introduced and then caught myself, before you saw it**: my first version of the portal's request logger used `req.path`. Express rewrites `req.url`/`req.path` relative to a mount point (`app.use("/api", requireAuth(...))`) and only restores it when the mounted handler calls `next()` — since a 401 never calls `next()`, every unauthorized request was logging `path: "/patients"` instead of `"/api/patients"`. Caught it by actually reading the test output rather than just checking the pass/fail count. Fixed by reading `req.originalUrl` (set once, never rewritten) instead. Both the reasoning and the fix are in a comment in `app.js` now, and the "after" test output above shows the corrected paths.
2. **A possible correction to FINDINGS.md's INFRA-03** (no `.dockerignore` bakes `.env` into images): re-checking while writing the `.dockerignore`s — `docker-compose.yml` sets `build: ./portal` / `build: ./notifier`, so each Dockerfile's build *context* is that service's own subdirectory. The root-level `.env` was never actually inside either build context, so `COPY . .` couldn't have copied it in via that mechanism as the finding describes. The `.dockerignore`s are still worth having (they stop `node_modules`/`.git`/stray local `.env` files placed *inside* a service directory from bloating or leaking into an image), but the specific "COPY . . bakes .env into the image" claim in the committed FINDINGS.md is inaccurate as written. Flagging since you already committed that file — didn't touch it myself since it's out of scope for this task and already agreed.

Everything else is as scoped: didn't touch `migrations/`, `docker-compose.yml`, `infra/`, `scripts/deploy.sh`, `README.md`, or either Dockerfile beyond adding the two `.dockerignore` files. `git status --short` confirms no other files changed and nothing staged/committed.

Task 3: containers, a migration runner and one-command local bring-up. I reviewed and committed your task 2 work in 4 commits. You were right about INFRA-03, I corrected it. Two fixes from my review go first:

2. The pg Pool has no 'error' listener. Neon scales to zero and drops idle connections, and an unhandled pool 'error' event kills the Node process. Add pool.on('error') that logs and carries on. Also read the pool size from PG_POOL_MAX (default 5); Lambda will set it low.

Migration runner

It needs a schema_migrations table, applies each pending file in its own transaction with ON_ERROR_STOP, and sets PGOPTIONS lock_timeout=5s and statement_timeout=60s so a migration fails fast instead of queueing behind the notifier.

#!/bin/sh
# Applies migrations/*.sql in order, each in its own transaction, using
# psql from the postgres image. This script assumes `psql` is already on
# PATH — it's meant to run inside a container built FROM the postgres
# image (see the `migrate` service in docker-compose.yml for the local
# path), or the same way by hand against a real database:
#
#   docker run --rm -e DATABASE_URL=postgresql://owner@host/db \
#     -v "$(pwd)/migrations:/migrations:ro" -v "$(pwd)/scripts:/scripts:ro" \
#     postgres:18-alpine sh /scripts/migrate.sh
#
# Run as the schema owner, never as portal_app/notifier_app — those are
# least-privilege runtime roles (see migrations/004_app_role_grants.sql),
# they don't own the schema and shouldn't be running DDL.
#
# --baseline <version>
#   Marks every migration up to and including <version> as applied in
#   schema_migrations WITHOUT running its SQL, then exits. For a database
#   that was already brought to that state by hand.
#
#   That is exactly the real prod DB: 001_init.sql and 002_add_index.sql
#   were applied by hand against it before this runner existed (see
#   RUNBOOK.md and infra/PROVISIONING.md). The first real run of this
#   script against prod should be:
#
#     ./scripts/migrate.sh --baseline 002_add_index
#
#   which records 001 and 002 as applied without touching prod's already-
#   correct schema. A normal run afterwards applies whatever comes next
#   (skipping 003 until it's fixed — see FINDINGS.md DATA-01/DATA-02).
set -eu

MIGRATIONS_DIR="${MIGRATIONS_DIR:-/migrations}"
: "${DATABASE_URL:?DATABASE_URL is required}"

# Fail fast instead of queueing behind a long-running notifier query.
export PGOPTIONS="-c lock_timeout=5000 -c statement_timeout=60000"

psql_c() {
  psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 "$@"
}

echo "==> ensuring schema_migrations exists"
psql_c -c "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_migrations (version text PRIMARY KEY, applied_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now());"

applied="$(psql_c -Atqc "SELECT version FROM schema_migrations ORDER BY version;")"

is_applied() {
  printf '%s\n' "$applied" | grep -qx "$1"
}

BASELINE=""
if [ "${1:-}" = "--baseline" ]; then
  BASELINE="${2:?--baseline requires a version, e.g. --baseline 002_add_index}"
fi

resolve_version() {
  needle="$1"
  match=""
  for path in "$MIGRATIONS_DIR"/*.sql; do
    stem="$(basename "$path" .sql)"
    case "$stem" in
      "$needle" | "$needle"_*)
        if [ -n "$match" ] && [ "$match" != "$stem" ]; then
          echo "ambiguous --baseline value '$needle': matches both $match and $stem" >&2
          exit 1
        fi
        match="$stem"
        ;;
    esac
  done
  if [ -z "$match" ]; then
    echo "no migration matches --baseline value '$needle'" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "$match"
}

if [ -n "$BASELINE" ]; then
  target="$(resolve_version "$BASELINE")"
  echo "==> baselining up to and including $target (recording only, not executing)"
  for path in "$MIGRATIONS_DIR"/*.sql; do
    stem="$(basename "$path" .sql)"
    if is_applied "$stem"; then
      echo "    $stem already applied"
    else
      echo "    baseline: $stem"
      psql_c -c "INSERT INTO schema_migrations (version) VALUES ('$stem');"
      applied="$(printf '%s\n%s' "$applied" "$stem")"
    fi
    [ "$stem" = "$target" ] && break
  done
  echo "==> baseline complete"
  exit 0
fi

for path in "$MIGRATIONS_DIR"/*.sql; do
  stem="$(basename "$path" .sql)"
  if is_applied "$stem"; then
    echo "==> $stem already applied, skipping"
    continue
  fi
  echo "==> applying $stem"
  psql_c -c "BEGIN;" -f "$path" -c "INSERT INTO schema_migrations (version) VALUES ('$stem'); COMMIT;"
done

echo "==> done"

#!/bin/sh
# Applies migrations/*.sql in order, each in its own transaction, using
# psql from the postgres image. This script assumes `psql` is already on
# PATH — it's meant to run inside a container built FROM the postgres
# image (see the `migrate` service in docker-compose.yml for the local
# path), or the same way by hand against a real database:
#
#   docker run --rm -e DATABASE_URL=postgresql://owner@host/db \
#     -v "$(pwd)/migrations:/migrations:ro" -v "$(pwd)/scripts:/scripts:ro" \
#     postgres:18-alpine sh /scripts/migrate.sh
#
# Run as the schema owner, never as portal_app/notifier_app — those are
# least-privilege runtime roles (see migrations/004_app_role_grants.sql),
# they don't own the schema and shouldn't be running DDL.
#
# --baseline <version>
#   Marks every migration up to and including <version> as applied in
#   schema_migrations WITHOUT running its SQL, then exits. For a database
#   that was already brought to that state by hand.
#
#   That is exactly the real prod DB: 001_init.sql and 002_add_index.sql
#   were applied by hand against it before this runner existed (see
#   RUNBOOK.md and infra/PROVISIONING.md). The first real run of this
#   script against prod should be:
#
#     ./scripts/migrate.sh --baseline 002_add_index
#
#   which records 001 and 002 as applied without touching prod's already-
#   correct schema. A normal run afterwards applies whatever comes next
#   (skipping 003 until it's fixed — see FINDINGS.md DATA-01/DATA-02).
set -eu

MIGRATIONS_DIR="${MIGRATIONS_DIR:-/migrations}"
: "${DATABASE_URL:?DATABASE_URL is required}"

# Fail fast instead of queueing behind a long-running notifier query.
export PGOPTIONS="-c lock_timeout=5000 -c statement_timeout=60000"

psql_c() {
  psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 "$@"
}

echo "==> ensuring schema_migrations exists"
psql_c -c "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_migrations (version text PRIMARY KEY, applied_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now());"

applied="$(psql_c -Atqc "SELECT version FROM schema_migrations ORDER BY version;")"

is_applied() {
  printf '%s\n' "$applied" | grep -qx "$1"
}

BASELINE=""
if [ "${1:-}" = "--baseline" ]; then
  BASELINE="${2:?--baseline requires a version, e.g. --baseline 002_add_index}"
fi

resolve_version() {
  needle="$1"
  match=""
  for path in "$MIGRATIONS_DIR"/*.sql; do
    stem="$(basename "$path" .sql)"
    case "$stem" in
      "$needle" | "$needle"_*)
        if [ -n "$match" ] && [ "$match" != "$stem" ]; then
          echo "ambiguous --baseline value '$needle': matches both $match and $stem" >&2
          exit 1
        fi
        match="$stem"
        ;;
    esac
  done
  if [ -z "$match" ]; then
    echo "no migration matches --baseline value '$needle'" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "$match"
}

if [ -n "$BASELINE" ]; then
  target="$(resolve_version "$BASELINE")"
  echo "==> baselining up to and including $target (recording only, not executing)"
  for path in "$MIGRATIONS_DIR"/*.sql; do
    stem="$(basename "$path" .sql)"
    if is_applied "$stem"; then
      echo "    $stem already applied"
    else
      echo "    baseline: $stem"
      psql_c -c "INSERT INTO schema_migrations (version) VALUES ('$stem');"
      applied="$(printf '%s\n%s' "$applied" "$stem")"
    fi
    [ "$stem" = "$target" ] && break
  done
  echo "==> baseline complete"
  exit 0
fi

for path in "$MIGRATIONS_DIR"/*.sql; do
  stem="$(basename "$path" .sql)"
  if is_applied "$stem"; then
    echo "==> $stem already applied, skipping"
    continue
  fi
  echo "==> applying $stem"
  psql_c -c "BEGIN;" -f "$path" -c "INSERT INTO schema_migrations (version) VALUES ('$stem'); COMMIT;"

"""
Load synthetic patients and a few queued reminders so the app has something
to show. Deterministic. No real person appears here.

    python3 scripts/seed_db.py
"""
import os
import random
import datetime

import psycopg2

DB = dict(
    host=os.environ.get("DB_HOST", "127.0.0.1"),
    port=int(os.environ.get("DB_PORT", "5432")),
    user=os.environ.get("DB_USER", "postgres"),
    password=os.environ.get("DB_PASSWORD", "postgres"),
    dbname=os.environ.get("DB_NAME", "wellis"),
)

FIRST = ["Sanne", "Jeroen", "Fatima", "Daan", "Emma", "Mohammed", "Sophie",
         "Lucas", "Julia", "Sven", "Noor", "Bram", "Isa", "Thijs", "Yara"]
LAST = ["de Vries", "Jansen", "Bakker", "Visser", "Smit", "Meijer", "Mulder",
        "de Boer", "Bos", "Vos", "Peters", "Hendriks", "Dekker", "Brouwer"]

random.seed(20260731)


def main():
    conn = psycopg2.connect(**DB)
    cur = conn.cursor()
    cur.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM patients")
    if cur.fetchone()[0] > 0:
        print("patients already loaded, skipping")
        return
    rows = []
    for i in range(2600):
        fn = random.choice(FIRST)
        ln = random.choice(LAST)
        name = f"{fn} {ln}"
        email = f"{fn.lower()}.{ln.split()[-1].lower()}{i}@example.com"
        dob = datetime.date(random.randint(1955, 2006), random.randint(1, 12),
                            random.randint(1, 28))
        phone = f"+3161{random.randint(1000000, 9999999)}"
        rows.append((name, email, dob, phone))
    cur.executemany(
        "INSERT INTO patients (full_name, email, dob, phone) VALUES (%s,%s,%s,%s)",
        rows,
    )
    cur.execute("SELECT id FROM patients ORDER BY random() LIMIT 40")
    ids = [r[0] for r in cur.fetchall()]
    now = datetime.datetime.now()
    for pid in ids:
        cur.execute(
            "INSERT INTO reminders (patient_id, channel, send_at, status) "
            "VALUES (%s, 'email', %s, 'queued')",
            (pid, now + datetime.timedelta(hours=random.randint(1, 72))),
        )
    conn.commit()
    print(f"seeded {len(rows)} patients and {len(ids)} queued reminders")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Local stack. No .env file required — every value here is either a
# throwaway dev credential (never used anywhere but this compose network)
# or a placeholder that's safe to commit. Real secrets live in the deploy
# target's secret store, never here.
#
# db (owner) -> migrate (owner, DDL/grants) -> seed (owner, fixture data)
#            -> portal / notifier (least-privilege app roles)
version: "3.9"

services:
  db:
    image: postgres:18-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
      POSTGRES_DB: wellis
    ports:
      # Loopback only — this used to be 0.0.0.0, reachable from anywhere
      # (see FINDINGS.md SEC-03). A GUI on the same machine can still
      # reach it on 127.0.0.1:5432.
      - "127.0.0.1:5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      # Local-only: creates portal_app/notifier_app. Only runs once, on
      # first init of an empty data dir. See db/init/01_roles.sql.
      - ./db/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U postgres -d wellis"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 5s

  # One-shot: applies migrations/*.sql (including the role grants) as the
  # owner, then exits. Nothing else starts until this succeeds.
  migrate:
    image: postgres:18-alpine
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    volumes:
      - ./migrations:/migrations:ro
      - ./scripts:/scripts:ro
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:postgres@db:5432/wellis
    entrypoint: ["sh", "/scripts/migrate.sh"]

  # One-shot: loads the synthetic demo data (skips itself if already
  # loaded). Runs as the owner — it inserts into patients, which the app
  # roles can't (they're read-only there by design).
  seed:
    build: ./notifier
    depends_on:
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    volumes:
      - ./scripts:/scripts:ro
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:postgres@db:5432/wellis
    entrypoint: ["python", "/scripts/seed_db.py"]

  portal:
    build: ./portal
    depends_on:
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      seed:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://portal_app:portal_app_dev_password@db:5432/wellis
      PORT: 8080
      # Fixed LOCAL-ONLY dev token, not a secret: raw value is
      # "[REDACTED:DEV_TOKEN]" (see README's curl example). name:sha256hex —
      # see portal/src/auth.js.
      API_TOKENS: "local:[REDACTED:DEV_TOKEN_SHA256]"
      # No MESSAGING_URL set for notifier, but portal has nothing to do
      # with sending — left here only as documentation that the pair
      # (portal, notifier) share the "no real provider locally" posture.
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8080:8080"
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--no-verbose", "--tries=1", "--spider", "http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 5s

  notifier:
    build: ./notifier
    depends_on:
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://notifier_app:notifier_app_dev_password@db:5432/wellis
      # Empty -> dry-run: logs what it would send and marks reminders
      # sent, instead of calling a real provider. We have no real
      # provider locally (or, currently, at all).
      MESSAGING_URL: ""
      MESSAGING_KEY: ""
      # Unset -> no receipts written. No default bucket, on purpose.
      RECEIPT_BUCKET: ""
    # The image's own CMD is the Lambda handler entrypoint, which expects
    # the Lambda Runtime API and just hangs locally. Override it to run
    # the polling loop instead.
    entrypoint: ["python", "notifier.py"]
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "sh", "-c", "tr '\\0' ' ' < /proc/1/cmdline | grep -q notifier.py"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 5s

volumes:

# throwaway dev credential (never used anywhere but this compose network)
# or a placeholder that's safe to commit. Real secrets live in the deploy
# target's secret store, never here.
#
# db (owner) -> migrate (owner, DDL/grants) -> seed (owner, fixture data)
#            -> portal / notifier (least-privilege app roles)
version: "3.9"

services:
  db:
    image: postgres:18-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
      POSTGRES_DB: wellis
    ports:
      # Loopback only — this used to be 0.0.0.0, reachable from anywhere
      # (see FINDINGS.md SEC-03). A GUI on the same machine can still
      # reach it on 127.0.0.1:5432.
      - "127.0.0.1:5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      # Local-only: creates portal_app/notifier_app. Only runs once, on
      # first init of an empty data dir. See db/init/01_roles.sql.
      - ./db/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U postgres -d wellis"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 5s

  # One-shot: applies migrations/*.sql (including the role grants) as the
  # owner, then exits. Nothing else starts until this succeeds.
  migrate:
    image: postgres:18-alpine
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    volumes:
      - ./migrations:/migrations:ro
      - ./scripts:/scripts:ro
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:postgres@db:5432/wellis
    entrypoint: ["sh", "/scripts/migrate.sh"]

  # One-shot: loads the synthetic demo data (skips itself if already
  # loaded). Runs as the owner — it inserts into patients, which the app
  # roles can't (they're read-only there by design).
  seed:
    build: ./notifier
    depends_on:
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    volumes:
      - ./scripts:/scripts:ro
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:postgres@db:5432/wellis
    entrypoint: ["python", "/scripts/seed_db.py"]

  portal:
    build: ./portal
    depends_on:
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      seed:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://portal_app:portal_app_dev_password@db:5432/wellis
      PORT: 8080
      # Fixed LOCAL-ONLY dev token, not a secret: raw value is
      # "[REDACTED:DEV_TOKEN]" (see README's curl example). name:sha256hex —
      # see portal/src/auth.js.
      API_TOKENS: "local:[REDACTED:DEV_TOKEN_SHA256]"
      # No MESSAGING_URL set for notifier, but portal has nothing to do
      # with sending — left here only as documentation that the pair
      # (portal, notifier) share the "no real provider locally" posture.
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8080:8080"
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--no-verbose", "--tries=1", "--spider", "http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 5s

  notifier:
    build: ./notifier
    depends_on:
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://notifier_app:notifier_app_dev_password@db:5432/wellis
      # Empty -> dry-run: logs what it would send and marks reminders
      # sent, instead of calling a real provider. We have no real
      # provider locally (or, currently, at all).
      MESSAGING_URL: ""
      MESSAGING_KEY: ""
      # Unset -> no receipts written. No default bucket, on purpose.
      RECEIPT_BUCKET: ""
    # The image's own CMD is the Lambda handler entrypoint, which expects
    # the Lambda Runtime API and just hangs locally. Override it to run
    # the polling loop instead.
    entrypoint: ["python", "notifier.py"]
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "sh", "-c", "tr '\\0' ' ' < /proc/1/cmdline | grep -q notifier.py"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 5s

volumes:
  pgdata:

# --- fetch_due: due vs future reminders ---


def test_fetch_due_only_returns_due_reminders(conn, patient):
    patient_id, _ = patient
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    due_id = queue_reminder(conn, patient_id, now - timedelta(minutes=1))
    future_id = queue_reminder(conn, patient_id, now + timedelta(days=1))

    ids = {row[0] for row in notifier.fetch_due(conn)}

    assert due_id in ids
    assert future_id not in ids


# --- run_once: DB state transitions, HTTP layer monkeypatched out ---


def test_failed_send_leaves_reminder_queued(conn, patient, monkeypatch):
    patient_id, _ = patient
    rid = queue_reminder(conn, patient_id, datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(minutes=1))
    monkeypatch.setattr(notifier, "send_one", lambda rid, channel, email: False)

    counts = notifier.run_once(conn)

    assert counts["failed"] == 1
    assert counts["sent"] == 0
    assert reminder_status(conn, rid) == "queued"


def test_successful_send_marks_reminder_sent(conn, patient, monkeypatch):
    patient_id, _ = patient
    rid = queue_reminder(conn, patient_id, datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(minutes=1))
    monkeypatch.setattr(notifier, "send_one", lambda rid, channel, email: True)
    monkeypatch.setattr(notifier, "write_receipt", lambda sent: None)

    counts = notifier.run_once(conn)

    assert counts["sent"] == 1
    assert counts["failed"] == 0
    assert reminder_status(conn, rid) == "sent"

# Local stack. No .env file required — every value here is either a
# throwaway dev credential (never used anywhere but this compose network)
# or a placeholder that's safe to commit. Real secrets live in the deploy
# target's secret store, never here.
#
# db (owner) -> migrate (owner, DDL/grants) -> seed (owner, fixture data)
#            -> portal / notifier (least-privilege app roles)
version: "3.9"

services:
  db:
    image: postgres:18-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
      POSTGRES_DB: wellis
    ports:
      # Loopback only — this used to be 0.0.0.0, reachable from anywhere
      # (see FINDINGS.md SEC-03). A GUI on the same machine can still
      # reach it on 127.0.0.1:5432.
      - "127.0.0.1:5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      # Local-only: creates portal_app/notifier_app. Only runs once, on
      # first init of an empty data dir. See db/init/01_roles.sql.
      - ./db/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U postgres -d wellis"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 5s

  # One-shot: applies migrations/*.sql (including the role grants) as the
  # owner, then exits. Nothing else starts until this succeeds.
  migrate:
    image: postgres:18-alpine
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    volumes:
      - ./migrations:/migrations:ro
      - ./scripts:/scripts:ro
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:postgres@db:5432/wellis
    entrypoint: ["sh", "/scripts/migrate.sh"]

  # One-shot: loads the synthetic demo data (skips itself if already
  # loaded). Runs as the owner — it inserts into patients, which the app
  # roles can't (they're read-only there by design).
  seed:
    build: ./notifier
    depends_on:
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    volumes:
      - ./scripts:/scripts:ro
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:postgres@db:5432/wellis
    entrypoint: ["python", "/scripts/seed_db.py"]

  portal:
    build: ./portal
    depends_on:
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
      seed:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://portal_app:portal_app_dev_password@db:5432/wellis
      PORT: 8080
      # Fixed LOCAL-ONLY dev token, not a secret: raw value is
      # "[REDACTED:DEV_TOKEN]" (see README's curl example). name:sha256hex —
      # see portal/src/auth.js.
      API_TOKENS: "local:[REDACTED:DEV_TOKEN_SHA256]"
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8080:8080"
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--no-verbose", "--tries=1", "--spider", "http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 5s

  notifier:
    build: ./notifier
    depends_on:
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://notifier_app:notifier_app_dev_password@db:5432/wellis
      # Empty -> dry-run: logs what it would send and marks reminders
      # sent, instead of calling a real provider. We have no real
      # provider locally (or, currently, at all).
      MESSAGING_URL: ""
      MESSAGING_KEY: ""
      # Unset -> no receipts written. No default bucket, on purpose.
      RECEIPT_BUCKET: ""
    # The image's own CMD is the Lambda handler entrypoint, which expects
    # the Lambda Runtime API and just hangs locally. Override it to run
    # the polling loop instead.
    entrypoint: ["python", "notifier.py"]
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "sh", "-c", "tr '\\0' ' ' < /proc/1/cmdline | grep -q notifier.py"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 5s

volumes:
  pgdata:

Error: in 18+, these Docker images are configured to store database data in a
       format which is compatible with "pg_ctlcluster" (specifically, using
       major-version-specific directory names).  This better reflects how
       PostgreSQL itself works, and how upgrades are to be performed.

       See also https://github.com/docker-library/postgres/pull/1259

       Counter to that, there appears to be PostgreSQL data in:
         /var/lib/postgresql/data (unused mount/volume)

       This is usually the result of upgrading the Docker image without
       upgrading the underlying database using "pg_upgrade" (which requires both
       versions).

       The suggested container configuration for 18+ is to place a single mount
       at /var/lib/postgresql which will then place PostgreSQL data in a
       subdirectory, allowing usage of "pg_upgrade --link" without mount point
       boundary issues.

       See https://github.com/docker-library/postgres/issues/37 for a (long)
       discussion around this process, and suggestions for how to do so.
